```{r}
#Problem_1_(a)
if (!dir.exists("data")) {
  dir.create("data")
}
download.file("https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2015/DataFiles/AUX_I.xpt",
destfile = "data/AUX_I.XPT",
mode="wb"
)
download.file("https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2015/DataFiles/DEMO_I.xpt",
destfile = "data/DEMO_I.XPT",
mode = "wb"
)
AUX <- haven::read_xpt("data/AUX_I.XPT")
DEMO <- haven::read_xpt("data/DEMO_I.XPT")

intersect(names(AUX), names(DEMO))
merged <- merge(AUX, DEMO)
dim(merged)

```

```{r}
#Problem_1_(b)
merged$gender <- merged$RIAGENDR
merged$gender <- factor(
  merged$gender,
  levels = c(1, 2),
  labels = c("Male", "Female")
)
table(merged$gender, useNA = "always")

merged$citizenship <- merged$DMDCITZN
merged$citizenship[
  merged$citizenship %in% c(7, 9)
] <- NA
merged$citizenship <- factor(
  merged$citizenship,
  levels = c(1, 2),
  labels = c("Citizen", "Not a citizen")
)
table(merged$citizenship, useNA = "always")

merged$children <- merged$DMDHHSZA
merged$children <- factor(
  merged$children,
  levels = c(0, 1, 2, 3),
  labels = c(
    "No children",
    "1 child",
    "2 children",
    "3 or more children"
  )
)
table(merged$children, useNA = "always")

merged$income <- merged$INDHHIN2

merged$income[
  merged$income %in% c(77, 99,12,13)
] <- NA

merged$income <- factor(
  merged$income,
  levels = c(1:10, 14, 15),
  labels = c(
    "$0–4,999",
    "$5,000–9,999",
    "$10,000–14,999",
    "$15,000–19,999",
    "$20,000–24,999",
    "$25,000–34,999",
    "$35,000–44,999",
    "$45,000–54,999",
    "$55,000–64,999",
    "$65,000–74,999",
    "$75,000–99,999",
    "$100,000 or more"
  ),
  ordered = TRUE
)

table(merged$income, useNA = "always")
```

```{r}
#problem_1_(c)

merged$right <- merged$AUXTWIDR
merged$left <- merged$AUXTWIDL

merged$right[
  merged$right %in% c(555, 777, 888)
] <- NA

merged$left[
  merged$left %in% c(555, 777, 888)
] <- NA
merged$right <- as.numeric(merged$right)
merged$left <- as.numeric(merged$left)
merged$children_num <- merged$DMDHHSZA
merged$children_num <- as.numeric(merged$children_num)
merged$income_num <- as.numeric(merged$income)

# Model 1R: right ear, gender only
model_1R <- glm(
  right ~ gender,
  data = merged,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  na.action = na.omit
)

# Model 2R: right ear, all four predictors
model_2R <- glm(
  right ~ gender + citizenship + children_num + income_num,
  data = merged,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  na.action = na.omit
)

# Model 1L: left ear, gender only
model_1L <- glm(
  left ~ gender,
  data = merged,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  na.action = na.omit
)

# Model 2L: left ear, all four predictors
model_2L <- glm(
  left ~ gender + citizenship + children_num + income_num,
  data = merged,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  na.action = na.omit
)
# Exponentiate the estimated coefficients
irr_1R <- exp(coef(model_1R))
irr_2R <- exp(coef(model_2R))
irr_1L <- exp(coef(model_1L))
irr_2L <- exp(coef(model_2L))

# Combine the results into one table
irr_table <- data.frame(
  Term = c(
    "Intercept (exp)",
    "Female vs Male",
    "Not a citizen vs Citizen",
    "Children aged <=5: per recorded unit",
    "Household income: per category increase"
  ),
  Model_1R = c(
    irr_1R["(Intercept)"],
    irr_1R["genderFemale"],
    NA, NA, NA
  ),
  Model_2R = c(
    irr_2R["(Intercept)"],
    irr_2R["genderFemale"],
    irr_2R["citizenshipNot a citizen"],
    irr_2R["children_num"],
    irr_2R["income_num"]
  ),
  Model_1L = c(
    irr_1L["(Intercept)"],
    irr_1L["genderFemale"],
    NA, NA, NA
  ),
  Model_2L = c(
    irr_2L["(Intercept)"],
    irr_2L["genderFemale"],
    irr_2L["citizenshipNot a citizen"],
    irr_2L["children_num"],
    irr_2L["income_num"]
  ),
  row.names = NULL
)

# Display a formatted table
knitr::kable(
  irr_table,
  digits = 4,
  col.names = c("Term", "1R", "2R", "1L", "2L"),
  caption = "Exponentiated coefficients from the Poisson regression models."
)

# Calculate deviance-based pseudo-R-squared
r2_1R <- 1 - model_1R$deviance / model_1R$null.deviance
r2_2R <- 1 - model_2R$deviance / model_2R$null.deviance
r2_1L <- 1 - model_1L$deviance / model_1L$null.deviance
r2_2L <- 1 - model_2L$deviance / model_2L$null.deviance

# Combine model statistics
model_stats <- data.frame(
  Model = c("1R", "2R", "1L", "2L"),
  N = c(
    nobs(model_1R),
    nobs(model_2R),
    nobs(model_1L),
    nobs(model_2L)
  ),
  Pseudo_R2 = c(
    r2_1R,
    r2_2R,
    r2_1L,
    r2_2L
  ),
  AIC = c(
    AIC(model_1R),
    AIC(model_2R),
    AIC(model_1L),
    AIC(model_2L)
  )
)

# Display a formatted table
knitr::kable(
  model_stats,
  digits = c(0, 0, 5, 2),
  col.names = c("Model", "Sample size", "Pseudo-R²", "AIC"),
  caption = "Model statistics. Pseudo-R² is calculated as 1 minus residual deviance divided by null deviance."
)
```

```{r}
#Problrm_1_(d)

# Part (d)

# Test 1: Gender difference in IRR
summary(model_2L)

# Extract gender coefficient test
gender_test <- coef(summary(model_2L))["genderFemale", ]

gender_test

# Calculate IRR
exp(coef(model_2L)["genderFemale"])

# 95% confidence interval for IRR
exp(confint.default(model_2L)["genderFemale", ])


# Test 2: Difference in predicted values

# Keep other characteristics the same
newdata <- model.frame(model_2L)[rep(1, 2), ]

newdata$gender <- factor(
  c("Male", "Female"),
  levels = levels(model.frame(model_2L)$gender)
)

# Predicted left ear width
predicted <- predict(
  model_2L,
  newdata = newdata,
  type = "response"
)

predicted

# Difference between female and male
predicted[2] - predicted[1]


```

```{r}
#Problrm_2_(a)
if (!dir.exists("data")) {
  dir.create("data")
}
download.file(
  url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bradleygrant/sakila-sqlite3/main/sakila_master.db",
  destfile = "data/sakila_master.db",
  mode = "wb"
)
#Because we use SQL in Rstudio so we need use the library to connect the database
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)
connection <- dbConnect(
  SQLite(),
  dbname = "data/sakila_master.db"
)
dbListTables(connection)
#way 1 to solve the (a)，first select the all column of customer
customer <- dbGetQuery(
  connection,
  "SELECT * FROM customer"
)
library(dplyr)

result_a_1 <- customer %>%
  group_by(store_id) %>%
  summarise(
    total_customers = n(),
    #According to the Sakila, active: 1 = active customer, 0 = inactive customer
    active_percentage = mean(active == 1) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

result_a_1
#Store 1 has 326 customers, of whom 97.55% are active. Store 2 has 273 customers, of whom 97.44% are active.

#Using way 2 to slove the (a)
result_a_2 <- dbGetQuery(
  connection,
  "
  SELECT
    store_id,
    COUNT(*) AS total_customers,
    AVG(active = 1) * 100 AS active_percentage
  FROM customer
  GROUP BY store_id
  ORDER BY store_id
  "
)

result_a_2
#the result same as result_a_1 that use way 1
#compare with these two 
library(microbenchmark)

compare_a <- microbenchmark(
  method_1 = {
    customer <- dbGetQuery(
      connection,
      "SELECT * FROM customer"
    )

    customer %>%
      group_by(store_id) %>%
      summarise(
        total_customers = n(),
        active_percentage = mean(active == 1) * 100,
        .groups = "drop"
      )
  },

  method_2 = dbGetQuery(
    connection,
    "SELECT store_id,
            COUNT(*) AS total_customers,
            AVG(active = 1) * 100 AS active_percentage
     FROM customer
     GROUP BY store_id
     ORDER BY store_id"
  ),

  times = 100
)

compare_a
```

```{r}
#Problem 2 (b)
#First use way 1 to slove the question
#select the data from SQL 
# Problem 2(b): Method 1

staff <- dbGetQuery(
  connection,
  "SELECT staff_id, first_name, last_name, address_id FROM staff"
)

address <- dbGetQuery(
  connection,
  "SELECT address_id, city_id FROM address"
)

city <- dbGetQuery(
  connection,
  "SELECT city_id, country_id FROM city"
)

country <- dbGetQuery(
  connection,
  "SELECT country_id, country FROM country"
)
#Since we don't know if the employees' addresses, cities and countries can be matched, we use left_join to ensure that each one is presented.
result_b_1 <- staff %>%
  left_join(address, by = "address_id") %>%
  left_join(city, by = "city_id") %>%
  left_join(country, by = "country_id") %>%
  select(staff_id, first_name, last_name, country) %>%
  arrange(staff_id)

result_b_1

#Using the way2 to solve the question
result_b_2 <- dbGetQuery(
  connection,
  "
  SELECT
    s.staff_id,
    s.first_name,
    s.last_name,
    co.country
  FROM staff AS s
  LEFT JOIN address AS a
    ON s.address_id = a.address_id
  LEFT JOIN city AS ci
    ON a.city_id = ci.city_id
  LEFT JOIN country AS co
    ON ci.country_id = co.country_id
  ORDER BY s.staff_id
  "
)

result_b_2
#Now compare these two ways
compare_b <- microbenchmark(
  method_1 = {
    staff <- dbGetQuery(
      connection,
      "SELECT staff_id, first_name, last_name, address_id FROM staff"
    )
    address <- dbGetQuery(
      connection,
      "SELECT address_id, city_id FROM address"
    )
    city <- dbGetQuery(
      connection,
      "SELECT city_id, country_id FROM city"
    )
    country <- dbGetQuery(
      connection,
      "SELECT country_id, country FROM country"
    )

    staff %>%
      left_join(address, by = "address_id") %>%
      left_join(city, by = "city_id") %>%
      left_join(country, by = "country_id") %>%
      select(staff_id, first_name, last_name, country) %>%
      arrange(staff_id)
  },

  method_2 = {
    dbGetQuery(
      connection,
      "
      SELECT
        s.staff_id,
        s.first_name,
        s.last_name,
        co.country
      FROM staff AS s
      LEFT JOIN address AS a
        ON s.address_id = a.address_id
      LEFT JOIN city AS ci
        ON a.city_id = ci.city_id
      LEFT JOIN country AS co
        ON ci.country_id = co.country_id
      ORDER BY s.staff_id
      "
    )
  },

  times = 100
)

compare_b
```

```{r}
#Problrm_1_(c)
#Firstly, use the way1 to solve the question-Select the data from SQL and then use R to calculate
payment <- dbGetQuery(
  connection,
  "SELECT rental_id, amount FROM payment"
)

rental <- dbGetQuery(
  connection,
  "SELECT rental_id, inventory_id FROM rental"
)

inventory <- dbGetQuery(
  connection,
  "SELECT inventory_id, film_id FROM inventory"
)

film <- dbGetQuery(
  connection,
  "SELECT film_id, title FROM film"
)
result_c_1 <- payment %>%
  inner_join(rental, by = "rental_id") %>%
  inner_join(inventory, by = "inventory_id") %>%
  inner_join(film, by = "film_id") %>%
  filter(amount == max(amount, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  select(title, amount) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(title)

result_c_1

#Using the using way 2 to solve the same question
result_c_2 <- dbGetQuery(
  connection,
  "
  SELECT DISTINCT
    f.title,
    p.amount
  FROM payment AS p
  INNER JOIN rental AS r
    ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
  INNER JOIN inventory AS i
    ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
  INNER JOIN film AS f
    ON i.film_id = f.film_id
  WHERE p.amount = (
    SELECT MAX(amount)
    FROM payment
  )
  ORDER BY f.title
  "
)

result_c_2

#compare with these two results
compare_c <- microbenchmark(
  method_1 = {
    payment <- dbGetQuery(
      connection,
      "SELECT rental_id, amount FROM payment"
    )
    rental <- dbGetQuery(
      connection,
      "SELECT rental_id, inventory_id FROM rental"
    )
    inventory <- dbGetQuery(
      connection,
      "SELECT inventory_id, film_id FROM inventory"
    )
    film <- dbGetQuery(
      connection,
      "SELECT film_id, title FROM film"
    )

    payment %>%
      inner_join(rental, by = "rental_id") %>%
      inner_join(inventory, by = "inventory_id") %>%
      inner_join(film, by = "film_id") %>%
      filter(amount == max(amount, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
      select(title, amount) %>%
      distinct() %>%
      arrange(title)
  },

  method_2 = {
    dbGetQuery(
      connection,
      "
      SELECT DISTINCT
        f.title,
        p.amount
      FROM payment AS p
      INNER JOIN rental AS r
        ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
      INNER JOIN inventory AS i
        ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
      INNER JOIN film AS f
        ON i.film_id = f.film_id
      WHERE p.amount = (
        SELECT MAX(amount)
        FROM payment
      )
      ORDER BY f.title
      "
    )
  },

  times = 100
)

compare_c
```

)

```{r}
#Problem_3_(c)
# Detect characters other than letters, commas, and whitespace
non_letter <- grepl(
  "[^[:alpha:][:space:],]",
  income$company_name
)

# Calculate the proportion
mean(non_letter)

# Also exclude ampersands
non_letter_no_amp <- grepl(
  "[^[:alpha:][:space:],&]",
  income$company_name
)

# Calculate the proportion
mean(non_letter_no_amp)
#Excluding commas and whitespace, 9% of company names contain a non-alphabetic character. When ampersands (&) are also excluded, the percentage decreases to 0.8%.
```

```{r}
#Problem_3_(d)
#delete the "-" first
phone1digits <- gsub("-", "", income$phone1)
phone2digits <- gsub("-", "", income$phone2)
#readd the "-"
income$phone1 <- sub(
  "^([0-9]{4})([0-9]{3})([0-9]{3})$",
  "\\1-\\2-\\3",
  phone1digits
)

income$phone2 <- sub(
  "^([0-9]{4})([0-9]{3})([0-9]{3})$",
  "\\1-\\2-\\3",
  phone2digits
)
head(income$phone1, 10)
head(income$phone2, 10)
```

```{r}
#Problem_3_(e)
#first choose the apartment
apartment_number <- grepl("[0-9]+$", income$address)
apartment_address <- income$address[apartment_number]
#select the umbers
apartment <- sub(
  "^.*[^0-9]([0-9]+)$",
  "\\1",
  apartment_address
)
apartment <- as.numeric(apartment)

#draw the graph
log_apartment <- log(apartment[apartment > 0])

hist(
  log_apartment,
  main = "Log of Apartment Numbers",
  xlab = "Log apartment number",
  ylab = "Frequency",
  col = "blue",
  border = "red"
)
```

```{r}
#Problem_3_(f)
apartment_positive <- apartment[!is.na(apartment) & apartment > 0]
#keep positive number
first_digit <- substr(
  as.character(apartment_positive),
  1,
  1
)

observed <- as.numeric(
  prop.table(
    table(factor(first_digit, levels = 1:9))
  )
)

expected <- log10(1 + 1 / (1:9))

comparison <- data.frame(
  digit = 1:9,
  observed = observed,
  expected = expected
)

comparison
barplot(
  rbind(observed, expected),
  beside = TRUE,
  names.arg = 1:9,
  col = c("red", "blue"),
  legend.text = c("Observed", "Benford"),
  xlab = "First digit",
  ylab = "Proportion",
  main = "First Digits of Apartment Numbers"
)
```
